title: Habit formation through continuing value
definition: Return visits come from the product continuing to deliver outcomes the user chose (a decision supported, a task completed, progress made), not from mechanics designed to bring them back.
intended_outcome: A returning user can say what they returned for, and the product helps them finish and leave.
implementation_guidance: Define value as outcomes against the user's stated goal: task completed, progress made, decision supported. App opens, session time, scroll depth, streak length and notification click-through are never targets (brain.dopemine.md section 2). They may be guard metrics only.

Reminders and notifications are opt-in, state the decision or task waiting and why now, are rate-limited and are easy to turn off. Copy names the decision needed, not just the event (brain.design.md section 2).
Progress displays show progress toward the user's declared goal. Breaking continuity carries no in-app penalty and no loss framing.

Apply the acid test of brain.dopemine.md section 2 to every proposed metric: describe a user for whom it improves while their life gets worse. If that user is easy to imagine, drop the metric or add a guard.
Every engagement-related recommendation this engine produces is flagged requires_human_review and goes through the Dopamine gate (brain.governance.md section 5) before adoption.

automated: Metric-proposal check against the prohibited-target list in brain.dopemine.md section 2 (a list lookup; proxy laundering still needs human review).
expert_review: Dopamine-gate review of any proposed mechanic, with the proxy trace of brain.dopemine.md section 3.
observed_behaviour: Return behaviour tied to an outcome event, as telemetry for diagnosis only.
customer_feedback: Ask returning users what they came back for.

limitations: Outcome-defined return is harder to measure than visits.
No claim that this produces habit is established for Dot products. This principle is a constraint plus a hypothesis, not a growth recipe.
Automated checks cannot detect proxy laundering.

evidence.summary: brain.dopemine.md section 2 prohibits raw session time, app-open counts, scroll depth, notification click-through as a terminal goal and streak length for its own sake as optimisation targets.
Dot Intelligence Manifesto non-negotiable rule 3: ethical engagement only; never optimise for addiction or screen time.
Return driven by delivered outcomes is more durable and less harmful than return driven by prompts.
evidence.rationale: A design stance, not a finding; no Dot measurement exists.

dopemine_constraint: Value is defined by user outcomes. Streaks, app opens, session time, scroll depth and notification click-through must not be optimised as targets (brain.dopemine.md section 2); proxies are traced per section 3; every engagement-related recommendation requires human review before adoption.
